Find the perimeter of a sector with radius 4 cm and angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians.
A circle has radius 5 cm. A chord subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians at the center. Find the area of the minor segment, using segment area = sector area minus triangle area.
questions.answer: Sector area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(5)^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\dfrac{25\pi}{4}$. Triangle area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(5)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\dfrac{25}{2}(1)=12.5$. Segment area $=\dfrac{25\pi}{4}-12.5\approx19.63-12.5\approx7.13$ cm$^2$.

questions.q: A circle has radius 6 cm. A chord subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radians at the center. Find the area of the minor segment, using segment area = sector area minus triangle area.
questions.answer: Sector area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(6)^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=6\pi$. Triangle area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(6)(6)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=18\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=9\sqrt{3}\approx15.59$. Segment area $=6\pi-9\sqrt{3}\approx18.85-15.59\approx3.26$ cm$^2$.

questions.q: Use the small-angle approximations $\sin\theta\approx\theta$ and $\cos\theta\approx1-\dfrac{\theta^2}{2}$ to approximate $\sin(0.1)$ and $\cos(0.1)$, to four decimal places.
Use the small-angle approximation $\tan\theta\approx\theta$ to approximate $\tan(0.2)$, and compare it to the exact value $\tan(0.2)\approx0.2027$.
questions.answer: $\tan(0.2)\approx0.2$ using the small-angle approximation. The exact value is $\tan(0.2)\approx0.2027$, so the approximation differs by only about $0.0027$.

sections.heading: Angular speed and radians per second

questions.q: A wheel rotates at 5 radians per second. Find the angle turned through, in radians, after 8 seconds, and convert this to the number of complete revolutions.
questions.answer: Angle $=5\times8=40$ radians. Number of revolutions $=\dfrac{40}{2\pi}\approx6.37$ revolutions.

questions.q: A wheel rotates at 3 radians per second. Find the angle turned through, in radians, after 15 seconds, and convert this to the number of complete revolutions.
questions.answer: Angle $=3\times15=45$ radians. Number of revolutions $=\dfrac{45}{2\pi}\approx7.16$ revolutions.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a swinging pendulum's arc

questions.q: This question has two parts. A pendulum of length 1.2 meters swings through an angle of $0.3$ radians on each side of vertical (a total swing angle of $0.6$ radians). (a) Find the length of the arc traced by the pendulum's tip during one full swing (from one side to the other). (b) Find the area swept out by the pendulum during this swing.
questions.answer: (a) Arc length $=r\theta=1.2\times0.6=0.72$ meters. (b) Area of the sector swept $=\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}(1.2)^2(0.6)=\dfrac{1}{2}(1.44)(0.6)=0.432$ square meters.
